_what: Ratchet pins for per-checker --self-test assertion counts.
_why: The SELFTEST_OK sentinel proves a --self-test RAN. It cannot prove the
self-test ASSERTED anything: gut the body of self_test() and it still
prints its sentinel and exits 0. A checker listed here must emit
'SELFTEST_OK <name> <n>' with n >= the pinned value, so assertions cannot
be deleted without the harness noticing.
Raising a pin is routine: add assertions, then raise the number in the
same commit. LOWERING a pin is the reviewable act -- it means a positive
control was removed, and the commit message must say which and why.
_how_to_migrate: 1. Have the checker's self_test() count its assertions (pass or fail).
2. Print 'SELFTEST_OK <name> <n>' on success instead of the bare form.
4. Prove it: delete one assertion, confirm selftest_validator.sh FAILS,
restore it. A pin never shown to fail is decoration.
_unmigrated_are_visible: selftest_validator.sh prints a coverage line naming every checker still on the bare sentinel, so the unmigrated set stays measured rather than assumed.
